title: Ammeter and voltmeter readings in a DC circuit with parallel branches

question.statement: An ideal ammeter (zero resistance) and an ideal voltmeter (infinite resistance) are connected as shown. The ammeter and voltmeter reading for $R_{1} = 5\,\Omega$, $R_{2} = 15\,\Omega$, $R_{3} = 1.25\,\Omega$ and $E = 20\text{ V}$ are given as

figure_refs.caption: Circuit diagram showing parallel branches with $R_1 = 5\,\Omega$ in series with an ammeter, and $R_2 = 15\,\Omega$, connected in series with $R_3 = 1.25\,\Omega$ and a parallel voltmeter across $R_3$, powered by an EMF source $E = 20\text{ V}$.
figure_refs.alt_text: Electrical circuit diagram with a DC voltage source of 20 V connected to a network. The network consists of a parallel combination of two branches: one branch containing resistor R1 = 5 ohms in series with an ideal ammeter A, and the second branch containing resistor R2 = 15 ohms. This parallel block is in series with resistor R3 = 1.25 ohms, across which an ideal voltmeter V is connected in parallel.
